issues.title: HPCM Software Forces Vehicle into Neutral While Driving (Recall 24S33 / 24V-330)
issues.description:
On affected 2022-2024 Maverick Hybrid trucks, 
a recent update to the Hybrid Powertrain Control Module (HPCM) software calibration may falsely set DTC U1010 and/or U1011 and result in a forced neutral condition while driving, causing the vehicle to coast to a stop and automatically shift to Park, along with a wrench light, multiple warning messages, and an audible chime. After shifting back into Drive the vehicle enters a limp home mode with limited torque at speeds up to 30 mph
. 
The powertrain controls team determined that new Hybrid Transmission Internal Park Module (HTIPM) software released for use in service in January 2024 was the cause, and Ford was aware of 315 warranty claims in North America as of April 15, 2024
.
issues.solution:
Dealers will reflash the PCM/HPCM with corrected software free of charge under recall 24S33. 
If the remedy software for Safety Recall 24S33 was not installed correctly during a prior dealership visit, the underlying forced-neutral condition may still exist
, so verify the calibration ID on the OASIS report — a follow-up recall (25V133/25S16) was issued for incorrect reflashes. 
If using a basic OBD reader you will likely see U1011 and U1028; full code set is U1010, U1011, U1028, U0418, U0401, U0131, which clear after the 24S33 update
. Repair is performed at no cost and takes under one hour.
symptoms: Vehicle suddenly shifts to Neutral while driving
Auto-shifts to Park as truck coasts to a stop
Wrench warning light illuminated
Audible chime and multiple IPC warning messages
Limp home mode limited to ~30 mph after restart
Truck strands driver and requires tow

communityRecommendations.content: If your truck unexpectedly drops into Neutral on the highway, pull to the shoulder and call for a tow — owners report limp mode prevents safe re-entry to traffic and the condition has recurred even after a dealer flash if the wrong calibration ID was installed.

After the 24S33 reflash, verify on your service receipt that the new HPCM calibration part number matches the year-specific Ford part (e.g. NZ6A-14C204-ZE for 2022, RZ6A-14C204-BC for 2024) — a botched flash triggered the follow-up 25V133/25S16 recall.

issues.title: Instrument Panel Topper Detaches During Airbag Deployment (Recall 25V884 / 25SE7)
issues.description:
On affected 2025 (and 2026) Mavericks, the instrument panel toppers may have been produced with insufficient vibration weld adhesion between the topper and the front passenger airbag chute door, allowing the instrument panel topper to detach during airbag deployment, which increases the risk of injury during a crash
. 
NHTSA is reporting a recall on 6,897 Ford Mavericks from the 2025 and 2026 model years where the instrument panel may detach when the air bags are deployed, potentially causing injuries to occupants — the fault is thought to affect 1% of vehicles from those model years
.
issues.solution:
Dealers will replace the instrument panel cover, free of charge. Owners should wait for communication from Ford which began January 19, 2026, with additional letters once the final remedy is available, anticipated February 2026
. 
Ford's part number for the subject instrument panel topper is SZ6Z-6004320
. 
Affected vehicles are 2025 Maverick units produced at Hermosillo Assembly between August 7, 2025 and September 5, 2025
 — check your VIN at the Ford recall portal or NHTSA.gov before scheduling.
symptoms: No driver-detectable symptom prior to crash
Possible dashboard rattle or loose-feeling IP topper in some non-recall units
Visible seam or gap at front-passenger IP topper edge (rare)

communityRecommendations.content: Do not delay this recall — the topper can become a hard plastic projectile during airbag deployment. Verify VIN even if your 2025 was not built in the Aug 7 – Sep 5, 2025 window, as Ford has expanded VIN lists on prior Maverick recalls.
Replacement topper part number is SZ6Z-6004320; ask the service writer to record the new part number on your RO so you have proof the correctly-welded remedy unit was installed.

issues.title: 8F35 Transmission Shudder/Buck/Jerk Below 35 mph and Output Carrier Bearing Wear
issues.description:
The 2.0L EcoBoost Maverick uses the same 8F35 eight-speed transmission found in other Ford applications, where 
vehicles equipped with the 8F35 transmission may exhibit a shudder/buck/jerk while driving up to 35 mph (57 km/h) due to software in the powertrain control module (PCM)
. 
A separate but related condition involves transmission slipping concerns, harsh engagements and various clutch DTCs (sometimes with torque converter clutch DTCs), caused by worn needle bearings in the output planet carrier assembly
. Drivers typically feel a low-speed shudder under light throttle, harsh 2-3 upshifts on hills, or a flare on the 4-5 shift.
issues.solution:
The correction is to follow the Service Procedure steps to reprogram the PCM and the transmission solenoid strategy
. 
After the adaptive strategy is reset, the computer begins a relearning process that may result in firmer than normal upshifts and downshifts for several days
. If shudder persists after the reflash, the planet carrier bearings may need overhaul — 
early 2022 EcoBoost Mavericks used 8F35 units built before Dec. 20, 2021, flagged for output planet carrier wear; shops keep finding slipping shifts, harsh D↔R, and metal glitter in the pan
. Reflash labor is ~0.9 hrs; a full overhaul including planet carrier, torque converter and valve body runs $3,500-$6,500 outside warranty.
symptoms: Shudder, buck or jerk between 15-35 mph
Harsh 2-3 upshift, especially on inclines
Slip or flare on 4-5 upshift under light throttle
Harsh engagement when shifting D↔R
Metallic debris in transmission pan
Delayed engagement when cold

communityRecommendations.content: Always have the dealer perform the PCM/TCM solenoid strategy reflash first — labor op 212389A, ~0.9 hours — before consenting to teardown. Drive the truck through several heat cycles and varied throttle conditions afterward to let the adaptive learn complete.

If you tow regularly or run AWD in heat, consider a drain-and-fill every 30,000-40,000 miles. The factory ULV fluid thins under sustained load, dropping line pressure and accelerating clutch glazing on the 8F35.

Persistent flare on 4-5 with metallic debris in pan points to output planet carrier wear (TSB 22-2281 family). The TSB-listed overhaul kit includes planet, bearings, Element A clutch housing, solenoid pack, and torque converter — do not piecemeal the repair.

issues.title: Engine Block Heater May Crack and Cause Underhood Fire When Plugged In (Recall 25SA4 / 25V685)
issues.description:
According to NHTSA, the engine block heater may develop cracks in its solder joints, allowing coolant to seep into electrical components. When the coolant evaporates, it leaves behind conductive salt deposits that can create a short circuit when the heater is plugged into a 110-volt outlet. A short circuit in the engine block heater increases the risk of an under-hood fire
. 
As of September 2025, Ford had received reports of 46 vehicles that experienced fires due to the block heater, with most incidents occurring in Canada; 4,277 2022-2024 Mavericks are included in the U.S. population
.
issues.solution:
The company will replace the faulty engine block heaters free of charge once newly designed parts become available
. 
Owners are advised not to plug in their block heater until the vehicle is remedied; dealers will replace the block heater free of charge. Owner notifications began October 24, 2025, and additional letters will be sent once the final remedy is available, anticipated February 2026
. Verify status using your VIN on NHTSA.gov under campaign 25V685 / Ford reference 25SA4. 
Risk increases when the block heater is plugged into an outlet without a functional circuit breaker or ground fault circuit interrupter
, so do not use the heater even briefly.
symptoms: Coolant residue or staining around block heater cord connector
Tripped breaker or GFCI when plugging in heater
Burning smell or scorch marks near front of engine bay
Underhood fire while parked and plugged in
Visible cracks at the block heater solder joint

communityRecommendations.content: Stop plugging in your block heater immediately — even if you have not received the recall letter yet. Ford has documented 46 fires, with most in Canada where block heater use is common. Park outside until the replacement part is available (anticipated Feb 2026).

If you must operate the vehicle in extreme cold without the heater, allow extra warm-up time and avoid hard acceleration until oil temperature comes up. Do not attempt to repair a cracked block heater yourself — Ford will replace it with the redesigned unit at no cost.
